ownership.notes: Samsung Group's holding-structure anchor. Four groups: Engineering & Construction (E&C — global EPC incl. data centers, BESS, HVDC, nuclear), Trading & Investment (T&I — owns the US solar/BESS development platform), Fashion, Resort. summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Samsung C&T is the third Hithium prospectus reference — and the most cautionary of the three. The relationship is real: a ~10 GWh 'global cooperation agreement' signed at Hithium's Xiamen HQ (announced Jan 6-8, 2025) with the E&C group, and the HKEX prospectus naming is confirmed (ess-news, Mar 2025). But 19 months on there is ZERO publicly attributed delivery — no named project, no volume drawdown, anywhere — and the partnership sits with the wrong arm for US purposes: Samsung C&T's US value pool is the Trading & Investment group's develop-and-sell platform (Samsung C&T Renewables — ~20 GW / 100+ projects across CAISO/ERCOT/MISO/PJM, ~$300M of cumulative sale gains 2021-2025), which exits pre-NTP so its BUYERS pick the batteries (Sunraycer, buyer of C&T's 3 GW Texas portfolio, chose Canadian Solar's e-STORAGE). Meanwhile the group's AIDC franchise is accelerating — Stargate Korea with OpenAI (floating data centers with Samsung Heavy), the Chuncheon and Haenam AI centers, a dedicated E&C Data Center Business Team, the LandBridge Permian BESS options on data-center-marketed acreage, and a stated intent to expand US development into AI data centers. Read: an unconverted optionality MOU pointed at E&C's non-US EPC theatre, attached to a group whose US machine is structurally FEOC-conscious.
ecosystemRole: We assess Samsung C&T as two different counterparties for Hithium: (1) the E&C group — a global EPC with genuine BESS execution (Melbourne Renewable Energy Hub 600 MW/1,600 MWh BoP+installation; 2.9 GWh executing in Australia; Guam solar+ESS; the Qatar solar franchise) where the 10 GWh partnership could plausibly convert in the Middle East, Australia, or Korea-adjacent markets; and (2) the T&I US platform — one of the largest non-IPP originators in ERCOT (land + interconnection positions at 20 GW scale) whose develop-and-sell model hands battery procurement to credit-sensitive US buyers, making it a channel Hithium influences only indirectly (by being specifiable in the projects C&T tees up). The group context cuts both ways: Samsung SDI's US ESS ramp (Indiana conversion, ~30 GWh target, $1B+ deals incl. 6.3 GWh to NextEra) creates latent sister-company pull toward Korean cells, while Korea's own battery politics lean domestic — but no C&T-SDI project pairing is documented either. The unconverted 10 GWh MOU is the account's defining fact: partnerships of this type frequently expire unexercised.

productsAndServices.name: US renewables development platform (T&I — Samsung C&T Renewables)
productsAndServices.description: Entered US solar development 2018; ~20 GW / 100+ solar and ESS projects across CAISO, ERCOT, MISO, PJM and the Southeast (company figures ranged 14.9 GW in 2023 → 23.2 GW in Mar 2025 → 20 GW current); regional bases: Cerritos CA (platform seat), Houston, Austin, Chicago, South San Francisco. Model: pure develop-and-sell exiting pre-NTP — site control, permitting, interconnection, PPA groundwork, then monetize the development rights, often retaining fee-based development services to NTP. Flagship: the Sep 2023 Sunraycer transaction — 15 Texas projects (~1 GW solar + ~2 GW ESS, 6,100 acres) sold with a development-services tail. Other documented: 150 MW Illinois solar to NorthStar Clean Energy (Aug 2023); Milam County TX ~700 MW (2021); LandBridge option-to-lease for two BESS totaling 350 MW in Pecos & Loving Counties, Permian Basin (Dec 2025, COD ≤ YE2028).
productsAndServices.positioning: Among the largest non-IPP originators in ERCOT — competing at the development-rights layer, not the IPP layer. Cumulative US sale gains ~$300M (2021-2025); $79M in 2025, ~$85M forecast 2026 — land-light, capital-light, lumpy by design.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bulk portfolio sales (Sunraycer), single-project sales (NorthStar), option-to-lease structures (LandBridge), plus post-sale development-services fees.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: US IPPs and platforms buying de-risked development positions.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Strategy shift under way: the LS ELECTRIC US JV (est. Feb 2025; first asset a 500 MW Texas BESS — MWh and supplier undisclosed) advances projects WITH a partner rather than flipping; stated intent to own/operate select projects, enter US EPC, and 'expand development capabilities into AI data centers.'

productsAndServices.name: Global EPC (E&C group) — where the Hithium partnership lives
productsAndServices.description: The E&C group is a top-tier global EPC (ranked #1 in Korea's Construction Capability Assessment 12 straight years): solar EPC franchise in Qatar (875 MW built + the 2,000 MW Dukhan award, Sep 2025, KRW 1.46T — ~80% of Qatar's solar once built), Guam 60 MW + ESS (completed), Australia (Melbourne Renewable Energy Hub — BoP + BESS installation contracts for 600 MW/1,600 MWh; 2.9 GWh of storage executing; Marinus Link HVDC KRW 470B), UAE HVDC, Barakah nuclear heritage, green hydrogen/ammonia. The Hithium agreement (Jan 2025): ~10 GWh of ESS execution projects worldwide — continuous supply of batteries + system solutions, streamlined supply chain; signed with E&C.
productsAndServices.positioning: The plausible conversion theatre for the Hithium MOU is E&C's non-US book (Middle East, Australia, Asia) — not the US, where E&C has no BESS EPC business and T&I's buyers procure independently.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EPC-for-hire (QatarEnergy-class clients); partner ecosystem: LS ELECTRIC (power systems), Hitachi Energy (European grid entry, Apr 2026), Siemens (infrastructure alliance incl. data centers, Nov 2025).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Sovereign/utility clients (Qatar, UAE), Australian renewables, Korean industrial.
productsAndServices.roadmap: E&C Q2 2026 operating profit KRW 202B (+71% YoY) — recovering from the 2025 high-tech project roll-off.

productsAndServices.name: AIDC platform (construction + group AI axis)
productsAndServices.description: E&C runs a dedicated Data Center Business Team (lifecycle: investment → design → construction → operations): 40 MW Hanam DC completed 2024; Ansan Global Cloud Center (40 MW, KRW 400B, IGIS Asset Management) secured 2025; expansion targets Malaysia, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia; $1B Ho Chi Minh City DC MOU (CMC). Group AI axis: Stargate Korea (Oct 2025) — Samsung C&T + Samsung Heavy Industries to jointly develop FLOATING data centers with OpenAI (first US floating DC engineering contract via SHI, initial installations planned for Texas); Chuncheon AIDC (C&T builds, Samsung SDS operates; 2.4 MW pilot, complete fall 2027); Haenam National AI Computing Center consortium (KRW ~2.5T, target Oct 2028). Cooling tech: proprietary immersion cooling (~80% cooling-electricity reduction claim), GRC partnership + Samsung Ventures investment. Also the constructor of Samsung Electronics' Taylor, TX fab — an existing Texas mega-execution footprint.
productsAndServices.positioning: Korea's most credentialed AIDC constructor with an OpenAI axis — but no US data-center project claimed to date; the US AIDC entry paths are the floating-DC program (Texas) and T&I's stated AI-DC development ambition.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Construction contracts (IGIS-class clients), consortiums (Haenam), group partnerships (OpenAI/SDS/SHI).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Korean and Southeast Asian hyperscale/AI operators; the OpenAI ecosystem.
productsAndServices.roadmap: The T&I land/interconnection machine pivoting toward data-center-adjacent power (LandBridge Permian positions sit on acreage marketed for digital infrastructure) is the connective tissue to watch.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess the Hithium-Samsung C&T relationship as real but unconverted: a prospectus-cited ~10 GWh global cooperation agreement with the E&C group that, 19 months on, has produced no publicly attributed project anywhere — the classic profile of an optionality MOU. Hithium's account priority should be conversion (a first named E&C project, most plausibly Middle East or Australia), because an unconverted flagship reference decays into a diligence liability at IPO scrutiny.

(High confidence) We assess the US leg as structurally misaligned: the partnership sits with E&C while the US value pool is T&I's develop-and-sell platform, whose buyers procure batteries post-sale under FEOC-era credit math — demonstrated by Sunraycer choosing e-STORAGE for the ex-Samsung Texas pipeline. Hithium influences this channel only by being specifiable (and FEOC-viable) in the projects C&T originates — which it currently is not for ITC-claiming vintages.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the LS ELECTRIC JV's 500 MW Texas BESS and the LandBridge Permian options as the two C&T-controlled US procurement events to track: for the first time C&T stays in projects past the flip point, meaning it (with LS) may actually issue a US battery PO — supplier undisclosed, timing 2026-2028, and Korean-partner dynamics (LS, plus latent Samsung SDI pull) favor compliant suppliers.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the group's AIDC axis (Stargate Korea, floating DCs with initial Texas installations, the Data Center Business Team, T&I's stated AI-DC development ambition) as the strategic reason to keep this account warm despite the unconverted MOU: if C&T becomes a US AIDC power developer, its land/interconnection machine plus the E&C-Hithium paper relationship is a ready-made channel — contingent on a FEOC-compliant Hithium offering.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: treat Samsung C&T as a conversion project, not a reference — push for a first attributed E&C project in a non-US market, monitor the LS JV's 500 MW supplier decision and Hithium's refiled prospectus customer tables, and recognize that Korean battery politics and Samsung SDI's US ESS ramp (~30 GWh target, NextEra 6.3 GWh) are the gravitational pull working against every future C&T battery decision.

The agreement — signed at Hithium's Xiamen HQ with the E&C group, announced January 6-8, 2025 — covers ~10 GWh of ESS execution projects worldwide with continuous battery-and-system supply, and the HKEX prospectus naming is confirmed. Yet no publicly attributed project exists anywhere: the classic optionality MOU.

The plausible conversion theatre is E&C's non-US book (Middle East, Australia, Asia — the Qatar/Dukhan-class franchise), not the US, where C&T's develop-and-sell T&I model hands battery procurement to its buyers (see the e-STORAGE/Sunraycer outcome) and Korean battery politics plus Samsung SDI's US ramp pull against every future C&T battery decision.
